Figure 8. Peak Memory consumption of ZeRO-2 and ZeRO-3 sharding strategies for Piper and TorchTitan. full copy of parameters and gradients across multiple microbatches and OOMs at batch size 8 for ZeRO-2 and batch size 16 for ZeRO-3. TorchTitan's PP x ZeRO-3 implementation also does not save significant memory compared to ZeRO-2.For Piper, we achieve correct resharding by reducing gradients after every backward pass instead of accumulating gradients between PP microbatches. This adds communication time compared to TorchTitan but achieves the full ZeRO memory savings. As a result, Piper is able to execute with much higher batch sizes than TorchTitan without OOM: 8x higher for ZeRO-2 (up to batch size 32) and 3.3x higher for ZeRO-3 (up to batch size 40).
